newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares close down on Wall Street, profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares close down on Wall Street, profit taking.

text.p: Italian shares closed mostly lower on Thursday, weakened by the slide on Wall Street and coinciding with a round of local profit-taking which put into reverse the bourse's gains in the run-up to the new year.
The blue chip Mib30 index finished 0.78 percent lower at 15,574 while the all-share Mibtel index was down 0.79 percent at 10,488.
"The fall in the Dow Jones index had an effect but the market was already overbought as a result of end-of-year window-dressing by domestic funds," said a Milan stockbroker.

Yellow pages company Seat was one of the star performers on the day of its market debut after its spinoff from state telecoms group Stet, finishing at 609 lire after opening at 550 lire. Stet was 0.44 percent off at 6,321 lire.
"The market has further to fall before it stabilises," said a Milan stock trader. Volume was thin at around 400 billion lire, accentuating the price fluctuations.

Shares in oil group ENI held up, ending the day 0.17 percent higher at 7,816 lire. Fiat took a dive, closing 2.41 percent lower at 4,461 lire as investors took profits after the stock had risen on the back of a government incentive scheme aimed at kick-starting Italy's languishing car market.
